items.title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining
items.summary_1line: The full-attention layers of large language models (LLMs) make every generated token more expensive than the previous one, slowing models down on long-context tasks. items.editor_note: Brings long-context cost into the thread, targeting the full-attention layers hybrid models keep, without retraining.

items.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding

items.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
items.summary_1line: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverage...

items.title: LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

items.editor_note: Latest entry: adapts long-context self-speculative decoding to looped Transformers with per-loop KV caches.

editorial.tldr: Speculative decoding research in late summer split between new drafters (diffusion draft trees) and context-heavy agent workloads (AsymSpec). Early November papers then went after the drafter itself: per-token reconsideration, block-diffusion fork trees, phrase-level drafting, and two losses that train directly for acceptance length.
editorial.whats_new: Callo (Nov 13) and LoopCache (Nov 18) move the thread to serving: Callo starts decoding agent requests whose KV cache was invalidated before re-prefill finishes, and LoopCache adapts self-speculation to looped Transformers' per-loop caches.
editorial.why_it_matters: For agent serving, the gap now named in papers is not draft quality alone but long or edited context, where KV-cache invalidation and re-prefill stall decoding under prefill-decode disaggregation.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agents edit context mid-session, measure re-prefill stall time on cache-miss requests before tuning drafters; drafter-level gains from these papers stay paper-only until they land in your serving stack.

beats.headline: Three papers rework how the drafter proposes tokens
beats.summary: Parallel reconsideration gives the drafter a second guess per token, DForkTree builds fork-aware trees from block-diffusion drafters like DFlash, and a phrase-level drafter proposes beyond the target's own vocabulary on a frozen target.

beats.headline: D-REAL and REAL Loss train drafters directly on expected acceptance length
beats.summary: Both argue token-level training objectives miss the quantity that sets the speedup, the number of consecutively accepted draft tokens, and optimize it directly.

beats.headline: Work shifts to long-context decoding and cache-invalidated agent requests
beats.summary: A retraining-free method targets the remaining full-attention cost in hybrid linear-attention models, Callo serves cache-miss agent requests under prefill-decode disaggregation, and LoopCache handles per-loop KV caches in looped Transformers.

open_questions: Does Callo's decode-on-invalidated-KV approach ship in an open serving stack such as vLLM or SGLang, or stay a research prototype?
Do acceptance-length losses like D-REAL and REAL Loss show up in released EAGLE-3 or DFlash drafter checkpoints?
Is there a reference implementation of AsymSpec or another context-aware method that agent-pipeline builders can benchmark?
Do the November drafter gains hold when measured against production serving baselines rather than each paper's own suite?
